title: Delhi Police Arrest Two Shooters, Foil Planned Attack on Bollywood Actor
excerpt: The Special Cell says Vikas Thakur and Deepak Singh were working for a foreign-based gangster, with a second alleged plot against a Delhi businessman in an extortion case.
body:
• Delhi Police's Special Cell arrested two alleged shooters — Vikas Thakur, 25, of Jalandhar and Deepak Singh of Tarn Taran — in separate operations in Delhi and Mumbai, police said.
  • Police say the men were tasked by a foreign-based gangster with shooting a prominent Bollywood actor in Mumbai; police have not named the actor.
  • A second alleged plot targeted a Delhi businessman in an extortion-related shooting, police said.
  • Deepak Singh was also wanted in Punjab in connection with the October 3 murder of Instagram influencer Mad Sandhu in Amritsar, according to police.

Delhi Police's Special Cell has arrested two alleged shooters and says it has foiled two planned shooting attacks — one on a prominent Bollywood actor in Mumbai and another on a businessman in Delhi — that were allegedly ordered by a foreign-based gangster.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (Special Cell) Narra Chaitanya said the two men were arrested in separate intelligence-led operations in Delhi and Mumbai, according to PTI's report in ThePrint. Police have not named the actor who was allegedly targeted, nor the foreign-based gangster said to have given the orders.

The two arrests

Police identified the arrested men as Vikas Thakur, alias Vicky, 25, a resident of Jalandhar in Punjab, and Deepak Singh, alias Deep, a resident of Tarn Taran district. According to police, Thakur travelled from Mumbai to Delhi on the gangster's instructions to carry out an extortion-related shooting targeting a local businessman, and Deepak Singh was expected to join him later; officers intercepted Thakur first. Singh was apprehended in Mumbai, where, police say, the gangster had instructed him to remain in order to facilitate the planned attack on the actor.

The alleged plot against the actor

Police say the planned shooting of the Bollywood actor in Mumbai was linked to remarks the actor allegedly made concerning the 1984 anti-Sikh violence, The Times of India reported. The arrests land in a period of heightened anxiety in the film industry over gang threats, which we covered earlier this week (Bollywood bolsters security as shootings revive underworld fears).

Singh was wanted in a Punjab murder case

According to police, Deepak Singh was allegedly involved in the October 3 murder of Instagram influencer Mad Sandhu in Amritsar, along with an aide, Palwinder, alias Kaka, on the same gangster's instructions. Palwinder was arrested by Punjab Police, while Singh evaded arrest and took shelter in Mumbai, police said. It was during that stay, according to police, that the gangster asked him to prolong his time in Mumbai to execute the planned attack on the actor.

Thakur's alleged path through the gangs

Police say Thakur entered crime as a juvenile in 2019 after a snatching incident, and allege that he began supplying illegal weapons to gangster Anmol Bishnoi in 2023. After Bishnoi's arrest, Thakur allegedly shifted allegiance to gangsters Anil Pandit and Randeep Malik, recruiting members, arranging firearms and conducting reconnaissance of extortion targets, before allegedly beginning to work independently for different criminal syndicates for money and coming into contact with the foreign-based gangster. India Today also reported both arrests and both alleged plots.

What happens next

IANS reported that a case under an FIR dated November 3, under Section 25 of the Arms Act, was registered at the Special Cell police station following Thakur's arrest, and that the operation was carried out by a team led by Inspectors Pankaj Chauhan and Suresh Chand Chaudhary under ACP Vivek Tyagi. Police have not publicly itemised any weapons recovered. Both men remain in custody as the Special Cell investigates the wider network, and the actor's identity — and any statement from the actor or their representatives — has not been made public.
